---
title: "Boundaries, approximations and numerical results"
description: "Separate the physical model, its geometric approximation and the numerical calculation."
scgsim-kind: "concept"
scgsim-status: "CONVERGING"
scgsim-id: "docs/concepts/model-and-numerics"
---

Three choices shape a result: the physical model, the representation of that
model, and the numerical calculation. Changing one is not the same as refining
another.

## Define the physical model

Record the conductor grounds, exterior boundary, substrate and vacuum extent,
port or junction elements, and material assumptions. Changing a grounded
conductor or junction inductance changes the experiment. Shared layout does
not imply matching exterior conditions: unspecified Palace Eigenmode uses its
natural PMC condition; the current source-first HFSS EPR model uses the recorded
HFSS default Perfect E exterior.

## Choose the geometric approximation

The solve geometry route decides how metal is represented; an approximation
profile decides how source geometry is interpreted physically. **Thin-Film**
(legacy code A) uses zero-thickness face-metal PEC sheets and finite bump/post
shells. **PEC Shell** (legacy code B) keeps the outer PEC boundary of finite
metal and excludes its interior from Palace tetrahedral solution domains. PEC
means perfect electric conductor, an ideal boundary model rather than a
measured conductor-loss model.

The `substrate_face` and `metal_gap_equivalent` profiles are physical-model
choices within Thin-Film. They differ in how the source film maps to the
solver geometry; changing the solve route does not automatically repair a
difficult mesh. The advanced **Retained Solid** geometry choice (legacy code C)
retains finite metal for polygon CAD, but is not a complete Palace Surface-EPR
route. See the [geometry reference](../geometry-sgb.qmd) for the route contract.

## Read numerical changes beside the quantity

Mesh size, geometric mesh order, finite-element order, adaptive passes, solver
settings and search controls determine different parts of the numerical
calculation. Palace's geometric order controls the mesh representation; FEM
order controls the field approximation. A native stopping flag describes its
configured criterion. It is useful alongside the actual changes in the
capacitance, frequency or participation you intend to use.

The 1.1.0 Palace mesh summary records the native mesh controls and
topology. Its Eigenmode degree-of-freedom value is a topology-based estimate,
not a native solver count or a convergence measure. The linear-tetrahedron
quality report also does not evaluate curved high-order element quality.

Keep the three high-order controls separate: `geometry_order` creates the mesh
geometry, FEM order controls the field approximation, and Palace
`HighOrderOutput` controls serialization. Palace's native import default
`RemoveCurvature=false` preserves imported high-order geometry nodes. For Palace Surface EPR, native Mask/Inset margins are separate evaluations from SGB geometry. The selected Palace executable must support Mask/Inset; see the [Palace Electrostatic contract](../specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#native-mask-inset). The former SGB geometry-distance-band producer is withdrawn.

An algebraic eigenpair residual and an adaptive mesh indicator describe
different quantities. A frequency can change little while a field-sensitive
surface contribution still changes. Inspect that contribution's available
history rather than borrowing confidence from a different observable.

::: {.callout-note title="Keep model and numerical comparisons separate"}
Refining a mesh investigates one model's discretization. Changing enclosure,
material or port assumptions investigates a different model. Label those studies
separately and retain units and mode/conductor identity when comparing results.
:::

A source preview displays declared geometry; a mesh/native readback displays
backend construction; a solved field supports physical postprocessing. Missing
sidewall energy or an unknown loss tangent remains missing or unknown, even if
other parts of the result are readable. Continue with
[EPR interpretation](../eigenmode-epr.qmd) or [result reading](../course/returned-results.qmd).
